forms: name the place of a digit
which digit is in the given place
MATH.G6.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.PLACE_VALUE.mastery: Given a whole number up to 9,999,999, the child names the place of any digit (ones to millions), including digits beside zeros, and says which digit is in a named place. Numbers in real settings such as a county population or a school budget.

forms: total value of an underlined digit
difference between two digits of the same value
build a number from total values
MATH.G6.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.TOTAL_VALUE.mastery: Given a whole number up to 9,999,999 the child gives the total value of a chosen digit (digit times its place) and writes the number in expanded form. The child does not confuse the total value of a digit with its place value.

forms: read a number aloud and write it
MATH.G6.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SYMBOLS_MIL.mastery: Given a number said or described in parts (for example 3 million, 45 thousand and 7) the child writes it in symbols with every place filled, using zero as a place holder. Numbers up to 9,999,999.

forms: spot the spelling or place mistake
MATH.G6.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.READ_WRITE_.mastery: The child writes a number up to 100,000 in words (British spelling, hyphen in twenty-one to ninety-nine) and writes a number given in words in figures. Limit as the design sets it: 100,000.

forms: order real quantities such as crowds or prices
MATH.G6.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ORDER_100K.mastery: The child orders a list of four to five numbers up to 100,000 from smallest to largest and largest to smallest, comparing digit counts first and then place by place from the left. Uses < and > correctly.

MATH.G6.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.ROUND_NEARE.mastery: The child rounds any whole number up to 100,000 to the nearest 1,000: looks at the hundreds digit, rounds 500 up, and keeps the answer in thousands (for example 49,500 rounds to 50,000).

MATH.G6.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SQUARES_TO_.mastery: The child works out the square of a whole number up to 100 as the number times itself (for example 40 squared is 1,600) and recalls the squares of 1 to 12 from memory. Squares of 13 to 100 are worked out, not recalled.

forms: side of a square from its area
is it a perfect square, and why
MATH.G6.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.SQUARE_ROOT.mastery: Given a perfect square up to 10,000 the child finds its square root and checks it by squaring. The child can say that a number such as 50 is not a perfect square because no whole number multiplied by itself gives 50.

forms: spot the mistake in a partial product
MATH.G6.NUMBER.MULTIPLICATION.MULT_4D_BY.mastery: The child multiplies a number up to 4 digits by a 2-digit number by the standard written method (two partial products, with zero placed in the ones of the tens row) or by partitioning, and solves a story that needs it. Products below 1,000,000.

MATH.G6.NUMBER.MULTIPLICATION.ESTIMATE_P.mastery: The child rounds both numbers to the nearest ten, multiplies the rounded numbers, and says whether an exact answer is sensible. Rounding to the nearest ten for both factors, as outcome b says.

forms: find the rule from a table
MATH.G6.NUMBER.MULTIPLICATION.MULT_PATTE.mastery: The child finds the rule of a pattern made by multiplying (for example times 2 or times 3), continues it, and finds a missing term. Terms do not exceed 1,000.

forms: spot the mistake in the working
MATH.G6.NUMBER.DIVISION.DIV_4D_BY_UP_TO_.mastery: The child divides a 4-digit number by a 1-, 2- or 3-digit number by long division, with the dividend greater than the divisor, gives any remainder as a whole number, and checks by multiplying back and adding the remainder.

MATH.G6.NUMBER.DIVISION.ESTIMATE_QUOTIEN.mastery: The child rounds the dividend and divisor to the nearest ten, divides the rounded numbers, and uses the estimate to check that an exact answer is sensible.

forms: spot the step done in the wrong order
MATH.G6.NUMBER.DIVISION.COMBINED_OPERATI.mastery: The child works out an expression with two or three of the four operations, doing multiplication and division before addition and subtraction and working left to right within each level, with numbers up to 3 digits. Brackets are taken first where they appear.

forms: add two fractions in a story
why we need a common denominator
MATH.G6.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.ADD_FRACTIONS_L.mastery: The child finds the LCM of two denominators (each up to 12), renames both fractions with it, adds the numerators, keeps the denominator, and simplifies. Sums that exceed 1 are written as a mixed number.

MATH.G6.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.SUBTRACT_FRACTI.mastery: The child renames two unlike fractions with the LCM of their denominators (each up to 12), subtracts the numerators, keeps the denominator, and simplifies. The first fraction is larger.

forms: change a mixed number to an improper fraction
spot the mistake in the conversion
MATH.G6.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.ADD_MIXED_NUMBE.mastery: The child adds two mixed numbers by adding the wholes and the fractions separately (using the LCM when the denominators differ) or by changing to improper fractions, and writes the answer in simplest form, renaming when the fractions total more than 1.

forms: spot the mistake when the fraction is too small
MATH.G6.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.SUBTRACT_MIXED_.mastery: The child subtracts one mixed number from a larger one, including the case where the fraction part is too small and one whole must be renamed, and gives the answer in simplest form.

forms: why has a whole number no reciprocal fraction written 0
MATH.G6.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.RECIPROCAL.mastery: The child writes the reciprocal of a proper fraction whose numerator and denominator are up to 2 digits by turning it upside down, and knows that a number times its reciprocal is 1.

forms: story about area of a square cloth
MATH.G6.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.SQUARE_OF_FRACT.mastery: The child squares a fraction with a one-digit numerator and a denominator of up to 2 digits by squaring the numerator and the denominator, and writes the answer in simplest form.

forms: write a score as a percentage
which fraction is the larger percentage
MATH.G6.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.FRACTION_TO_PER.mastery: The child writes a fraction as a percentage by making the denominator 100 or by dividing and multiplying by 100, including fractions with denominators that are factors of 100 and a mark out of a total.

MATH.G6.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.PERCENT_TO_FRAC.mastery: The child writes a percentage as a fraction out of 100 and simplifies it to simplest form.

forms: write the decimal from its words
MATH.G6.NUMBER.DECIMALS.DECIMAL_PLACES_T.mastery: The child names the place of a digit after the decimal point up to ten-thousandths, gives its value as a fraction, and writes a decimal from a place description (for example 7 ten-thousandths as 0.0007).

MATH.G6.NUMBER.DECIMALS.ROUND_DECIMALS_3.mastery: The child rounds a decimal to 1, 2 or 3 decimal places by looking at the next digit, including when the rounding carries across a 9 (for example 4.9996 to 3 places is 5.000).

MATH.G6.NUMBER.DECIMALS.DECIMAL_TO_FRACT.mastery: The child writes a decimal with up to 3 places as a fraction with denominator 10, 100 or 1,000 and simplifies it.

MATH.G6.NUMBER.DECIMALS.FRACTION_TO_DECI.mastery: The child writes a fraction as a decimal by dividing the numerator by the denominator or by renaming it with denominator 10, 100 or 1,000 (denominators such as 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 25, 50).

forms: story about a tank or a score
MATH.G6.NUMBER.DECIMALS.DECIMAL_TO_PERCE.mastery: The child writes a decimal as a percentage by multiplying by 100 (moving the point two places), including decimals less than 0.1 and more than 1.

MATH.G6.NUMBER.DECIMALS.PERCENT_TO_DECIM.mastery: The child writes a percentage as a decimal by dividing by 100 (moving the point two places left), including 5%, 0.5% and 120%.

forms: add several amounts in a story
MATH.G6.NUMBER.DECIMALS.ADD_DECIMALS_4DP.mastery: The child adds two or three decimals with up to 4 decimal places in columns with the points in line, filling empty places with zeros.

MATH.G6.NUMBER.DECIMALS.SUBTRACT_DECIMAL.mastery: The child subtracts one decimal from another with up to 4 decimal places in columns with the points in line, renaming across zeros and filling empty places with zeros.

MATH.G6.NUMBER.INEQUALITIES.FORM_INEQUAL.mastery: The child writes an inequality using <, >, at least, at most, from a short story (for example "at least 30 learners" as x >= 30 or "fewer than 12" as x < 12) and chooses the right symbol.

MATH.G6.NUMBER.INEQUALITIES.SIMPLIFY_INE.mastery: The child simplifies an inequality such as x + 5 < 12 or 3x > 18 in one step to x < 7 or x > 6 by doing the same operation to both sides, and keeps the symbol pointing the same way.

MATH.G6.NUMBER.INEQUALITIES.SOLVE_INEQUA.mastery: The child solves a one-step or two-step inequality, lists the whole-number solutions or the largest or smallest one, and checks a value by substituting. No negative multipliers or divisors.

forms: read a ruler to the nearest mm
which object is measured in mm
estimate a small length in mm
MATH.G6.MEASUR.LENGTH.MM_AS_UNIT.mastery: The child chooses the sensible unit (mm, cm, m or km) for a small length such as a coin, a pencil lead or a wire thickness, and reads a length to the nearest millimetre on a ruler.

forms: how many mm in a cm
cm and mm as a mixed length
MATH.G6.MEASUR.LENGTH.MM_CM_RELATIONSHIP.mastery: The child knows that 1 cm is 10 mm and uses it to say how many mm are in a number of cm and how many cm in a number of mm (whole and half centimetres), for example 25 mm is 2 cm and 5 mm.

MATH.G6.MEASUR.LENGTH.CONVERT_TO_MM.mastery: The child changes a length given in cm, or in cm and mm, to mm (multiply the cm by 10 and add the mm), for lengths up to 1,000 mm.

forms: story about a fence or ribbon
MATH.G6.MEASUR.LENGTH.ADD_CM_MM.mastery: The child adds two lengths in cm and mm, adds mm to mm and cm to cm, and renames 10 mm or more as cm, giving the answer as cm and mm.

forms: what is left of a ribbon
spot the mistake when mm are too few
MATH.G6.MEASUR.LENGTH.SUBTRACT_CM_MM.mastery: The child subtracts one length in cm and mm from a longer one, renaming 1 cm as 10 mm when the mm are too few.

forms: equal pieces laid end to end
MATH.G6.MEASUR.LENGTH.MULTIPLY_CM_MM.mastery: The child multiplies a length in cm and mm by a whole number (up to 12), multiplies each part and renames mm of 10 or more as cm.

forms: spot the leftover cm not renamed
MATH.G6.MEASUR.LENGTH.DIVIDE_CM_MM.mastery: The child divides a length in cm and mm into a whole number of equal parts (up to 12), changing to mm when the cm do not divide exactly, and gives the answer in cm and mm.

forms: read measured values from a table
use the pattern to find a missing value
which tool measures round the edge
MATH.G6.MEASUR.LENGTH.CIRCUMFERENCE_PRAC.mastery: The child reads a circumference measured with string or a tape (the length round the edge) and uses a measured table of circumference and diameter to work out a missing one, and the distance a wheel rolls in turns. The measuring itself is a hands-on task and stays with a practical.
MATH.G6.MEASUR.LENGTH.CIRCUMFERENCE_PRAC.hands_on: The practical measuring with string stays with the teacher; the questions test reading and using the measurements.

MATH.G6.MEASUR.LENGTH.CIRCUMFERENCE_DIAM.mastery: The child knows that the circumference of a circle is about 3 times its diameter (pi, with 22/7 or 3.14 given in the question), finds the circumference from the diameter and the diameter from the circumference, and knows that the diameter is twice the radius.

forms: story about a flower bed or a sail
MATH.G6.MEASUR.AREA.AREA_TRIANGLE.mastery: The child works out the area of a triangle as half of base times height in cm2, with the height at right angles to the base, and finds a missing base or height from the area.

forms: area of a shape with a triangle on top
MATH.G6.MEASUR.AREA.AREA_COMBINED.mastery: The child splits a shape made of squares, rectangles and triangles into parts, finds each part's area in cm2 and adds (or subtracts a cut-out), giving the area in cm2.

forms: why the answer is only an estimate
MATH.G6.MEASUR.AREA.AREA_CIRCLE_BY_COUNT.mastery: The child estimates the area of a circle drawn on squared paper by counting whole squares and adding half for the part-squares, and says the answer is an estimate.

forms: capacity of a cube of side 1 cm
a box of 1,000 cm3 holds how many litres
MATH.G6.MEASUR.CAPACITY.CM3_ML_LITRE_REL.mastery: The child knows that 1 cm3 holds 1 ml and that 1,000 cm3 (1,000 ml) is 1 litre, and uses this to say the capacity of a small cube or a box in ml or litres.

forms: story about bottles or a jug
MATH.G6.MEASUR.CAPACITY.LITRES_TO_ML.mastery: The child changes litres, or litres and millilitres, to millilitres (multiply the litres by 1,000, add the ml), including decimals of a litre such as 2.5 l.

MATH.G6.MEASUR.CAPACITY.ML_TO_LITRES.mastery: The child changes millilitres to litres (divide by 1,000) and gives litres and millilitres, or a decimal of a litre, for amounts up to 10,000 ml.

MATH.G6.MEASUR.MASS.TONNE_AS_UNIT.mastery: The child knows the tonne (t) as a unit for very heavy masses and that it is bigger than the kilogramme, and chooses g, kg or t for a stated object.

forms: choose the sensible mass for a lorry or an elephant
sort items into g, kg and t
MATH.G6.MEASUR.MASS.ITEMS_IN_TONNES.mastery: The child picks from a list the items whose mass is given in tonnes (a lorry, a heap of sand, a harvest of maize) and not those given in kg or g.

forms: how many kg in a tonne
which is greater: kg or t
MATH.G6.MEASUR.MASS.KG_TONNE_RELATIONSHI.mastery: The child knows that 1 tonne is 1,000 kg and uses it to say how many equal sacks make a tonne, for example how many 50 kg sacks.

forms: estimate the load of a lorry
estimate from the number of sacks
MATH.G6.MEASUR.MASS.ESTIMATE_TONNES.mastery: The child estimates the mass of a large load in tonnes from a familiar comparison (a bag of maize 90 kg, a lorry load of sacks) and chooses a sensible estimate.

MATH.G6.MEASUR.MASS.CONVERT_KG_TONNES.mastery: The child changes tonnes, or tonnes and kilogrammes, to kilogrammes (multiply by 1,000, add the kg) and kilogrammes to tonnes (divide by 1,000, giving t and kg or a decimal).

MATH.G6.MEASUR.MASS.ADD_TONNES_KG.mastery: The child adds two masses in tonnes and kilogrammes, adds kg to kg and t to t, and renames 1,000 kg or more as tonnes.

forms: what is left of a load
spot the mistake when kg are too few
MATH.G6.MEASUR.MASS.SUBTRACT_TONNES_KG.mastery: The child subtracts one mass in tonnes and kilogrammes from a larger one, renaming 1 tonne as 1,000 kg when the kg are too few.

MATH.G6.MEASUR.MASS.MULTIPLY_TONNES_KG.mastery: The child multiplies a mass in tonnes and kilogrammes by a whole number (up to 12) and renames kg of 1,000 or more as tonnes.

MATH.G6.MEASUR.MASS.DIVIDE_TONNES_KG.mastery: The child divides a mass in tonnes and kilogrammes into equal parts (up to 12), changing to kg when the tonnes do not divide exactly.

forms: a.m. or p.m. for an event
MATH.G6.MEASUR.TIME.AM_PM_IDENTIFY.mastery: The child says whether an everyday event (breakfast, assembly, evening news) happens in the a.m. or the p.m. and knows that a.m. is from midnight to noon and p.m. from noon to midnight.

forms: write the time with a.m. or p.m.
read a clock and write the time
MATH.G6.MEASUR.TIME.WRITE_AM_PM.mastery: The child writes a time shown on a clock or described in words with a.m. or p.m. (for example 7:30 p.m.), including 12 noon and 12 midnight.

MATH.G6.MEASUR.TIME.AM_PM_TO_24H_RELATE.mastery: The child matches times in a.m. and p.m. to the 24-hour clock (for example 3 p.m. and 15:00) and sees that the hours after noon are 12 more than on the 12-hour clock.

forms: spot the mistake at noon or midnight
MATH.G6.MEASUR.TIME.CONVERT_12_24.mastery: The child writes a 12-hour time in 24-hour form (add 12 hours to p.m. times other than 12 noon, 12 a.m. is 00:00) and a 24-hour time in 12-hour form with a.m. or p.m.

MATH.G6.MEASUR.TIME.TRAVEL_TIMETABLE.mastery: The child reads a table of departure and arrival times, in the 12-hour or 24-hour system, and works out the length of a journey, the waiting time and the shortest or earliest trip.

MATH.G6.MEASUR.MONEY.PREPARE_BUDGET.mastery: The child lists income and planned spending in a table, totals each, and finds the balance (income less spending) and whether the budget is over or under.

forms: selling price from cost and profit
buying price from selling price and profit
MATH.G6.MEASUR.MONEY.BUYING_SELLING_PRIC.mastery: The child tells the buying price (cost) from the selling price, works out the selling price from the buying price and the profit or loss, and the buying price from the selling price and profit or loss.

MATH.G6.MEASUR.MONEY.PROFIT_FROM_SALES.mastery: The child works out profit as selling price less buying price when the selling price is greater, for a single item or for a number of items bought and sold together.

MATH.G6.MEASUR.MONEY.LOSS_FROM_SALES.mastery: The child works out the loss as buying price less selling price when the selling price is less, and decides from the two prices whether the sale made a profit or a loss.

forms: which tax is taken from pay
take-home pay on a pay slip
MATH.G6.MEASUR.MONEY.TYPES_OF_TAXES.mastery: The child names common taxes in Kenya (VAT on goods, PAYE on pay, import duty, land rates) and says what each is charged on, and works out an amount of tax or a total when a rate is stated in the question.

forms: spot the pair that will meet
MATH.G6.GEOMET.LINES.PARALLEL_LINES.mastery: The child knows that parallel lines are always the same distance apart and never meet, picks them out from a set of lines in the environment (rails, ruled lines, a window frame), and says that a set square slid along a ruler draws them.
MATH.G6.GEOMET.LINES.PARALLEL_LINES.hands_on: Drawing or constructing is a practical done with a pencil and instruments; a typed or tapped question tests the idea behind it, not the construction.

forms: which step of the construction is wrong
MATH.G6.GEOMET.LINES.BISECT_LINES.mastery: The child knows that to bisect is to cut into two equal parts, that the bisector of a line meets it at its midpoint at a right angle, works out each half of a line of given length, and knows the compass arcs have the same radius on both ends.
MATH.G6.GEOMET.LINES.BISECT_LINES.hands_on: Drawing or constructing is a practical done with a pencil and instruments; a typed or tapped question tests the idea behind it, not the construction.

forms: which tool checks a right angle
MATH.G6.GEOMET.LINES.PERPENDICULAR_LINES.mastery: The child knows that perpendicular lines meet at a right angle (90 degrees), picks out perpendicular lines in the environment (wall and floor, a window corner), and says that a set square or a compass construction makes them.
MATH.G6.GEOMET.LINES.PERPENDICULAR_LINES.hands_on: Drawing or constructing is a practical done with a pencil and instruments; a typed or tapped question tests the idea behind it, not the construction.

forms: which angles are on a line
how many angles on a line
angles in a cut round cake at a point
MATH.G6.GEOMET.ANGLES.ANGLES_STRAIGHT_LI.mastery: The child picks out the angles that share a point on a straight line (they make a straight angle), and says that two or more angles on a straight line at a point lie along it, and names right, acute and obtuse ones.

forms: is the angle acute or obtuse?
MATH.G6.GEOMET.ANGLES.MEASURE_ANGLES_PRO.mastery: The child reads an angle on a protractor from the correct scale (starting from zero on the baseline) and finds the difference between two readings.
MATH.G6.GEOMET.ANGLES.MEASURE_ANGLES_PRO.hands_on: Placing the protractor on a real angle stays a practical; the questions test reading a drawn protractor.

forms: one angle is 4 times the other
MATH.G6.GEOMET.ANGLES.SUM_ANGLES_STRAIGH.mastery: The child knows that angles on a straight line at a point add up to 180 degrees and finds a missing angle (two or three angles, including an angle given as a multiple of another).

forms: sum of the angles of a rectangle
MATH.G6.GEOMET.ANGLES.ANGLE_SUM_RECT_TRI.mastery: The child knows that the angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees and the angles of a rectangle to 360 degrees (each 90 degrees), and finds a missing angle of a triangle.

forms: name the triangle from its sides
which triangle has a right angle
MATH.G6.GEOMET.ANGLES.CONSTRUCT_TRIANGLE.mastery: The child names a triangle from its sides and angles (three equal sides, a right angle, two equal sides), knows the angles of an equilateral triangle are all 60 degrees, and which sides are equal in an isosceles triangle. The construction itself is a practical.
MATH.G6.GEOMET.ANGLES.CONSTRUCT_TRIANGLE.hands_on: Drawing or constructing is a practical done with a pencil and instruments; a typed or tapped question tests the idea behind it, not the construction.

forms: missing angle of an isosceles triangle
other angle of a right-angled triangle
MATH.G6.GEOMET.ANGLES.INTERIOR_ANGLES_TR.mastery: The child finds an unknown interior angle of an equilateral, right-angled or isosceles triangle using that the angles add to 180 degrees, the angles opposite equal sides are equal, and the right angle is 90 degrees. Measuring with a protractor is a practical.
MATH.G6.GEOMET.ANGLES.INTERIOR_ANGLES_TR.hands_on: Drawing or constructing is a practical done with a pencil and instruments; a typed or tapped question tests the idea behind it, not the construction.

MATH.G6.GEOMET.3_D_OBJECTS.CUBOID_CUBE_P.mastery: The child counts the vertices (8), faces (6) and edges (12) of a cube or a cuboid, tells which faces are equal, works out the length of wire for the edges of a cube or cuboid, and matches a net to its solid.

MATH.G6.GEOMET.3_D_OBJECTS.CYLINDER_PART.mastery: The child says a cylinder has 2 flat circular faces, 1 curved surface and 2 curved edges, no vertices, and identifies cylinders in the environment (tin, pipe, drum).

forms: trace a face and name it
MATH.G6.GEOMET.3_D_OBJECTS.PLANE_FIGURES.mastery: The child names the plane figure that is the shape of a face of a solid (squares on a cube, rectangles on a cuboid, circles on a cylinder, triangles on a pyramid) and a solid that has a given face.

MATH.G6.DATA_H.BAR_GRAPHS.FREQUENCY_TABL.mastery: The child tallies raw data into a frequency table, adds the frequencies to find the total, finds a missing frequency, and says which value is the most frequent.

MATH.G6.DATA_H.BAR_GRAPHS.PICTOGRAPH.mastery: The child works out how many symbols a frequency needs when a symbol stands for more than one (2, 5 or 10), reads the key, and deals with half symbols.

forms: what does each counter stand for
MATH.G6.DATA_H.BAR_GRAPHS.PILING.mastery: The child says that in piling each object stands for one item counted, that the tallest pile is the most frequent, finds the total of all piles, and which pile has the fewest. The sorting and piling itself is a practical.
MATH.G6.DATA_H.BAR_GRAPHS.PILING.hands_on: Piling objects is a practical; the questions test counting and comparing piles.

forms: what is missing on the graph
MATH.G6.DATA_H.BAR_GRAPHS.BAR_GRAPH_DRAW.mastery: The child chooses a scale for the vertical axis, works out how many squares or what height a frequency needs, and says what a bar graph needs (a title, labelled axes, equal bar widths).
MATH.G6.DATA_H.BAR_GRAPHS.BAR_GRAPH_DRAW.hands_on: Drawing the graph on paper stays a practical; the questions test the scale and the heights.

MATH.G6.DATA_H.BAR_GRAPHS.BAR_GRAPH_INTE.mastery: The child reads values from a bar graph (including a scale that goes up in 2s, 5s or 10s), finds the difference between two bars, the total, and the second highest bar, and draws a conclusion.
